sections.title: Job aid for COVID-19 vaccine Administration
Janssen–Cilag International NV (Belgium) Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine

summary.text: Gives the international non-proprietary name of the Janssen Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine covered by this job aid.

sections.title: General information

summary.text: Summarises key facts on the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine: five-dose vials, a single 0.5 ml dose, use from age 18 and intramuscular injection in the deltoid.

sections.extract: GENERAL INFORMATION  Vaccine: Janssen Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine, multi-dose vial. Each vial contains 5 doses of 0.5 ml  Schedule: One dose of 0.5 ml  Age indication: 18 years of age and older  Route and site of administration: Intramuscular, in the deltoid muscle of the upper arm

sections.title: Storage conditionS and shelf life of vaccine

summary.text: Sets out storage conditions and shelf life for the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine, frozen for up to 24 months or refrigerated for up to 4.5 months, and stresses protection from light and no refreezing after thawing. It explains that opened vials must be used within six hours or by the end of the session, and how to record dates and update expiry dates when moving vials to the refrigerator.

sections.extract: STORAGE CONDITIONS AND SHELF LIFE OF VACCINE STORAGE CONDITIONS SHELF LIFE Unopened vaccine vials: Freezer: -25 °C to -15 °C 24 months by expiry date • Prior to use, avoid vaccine exposure to direct sunlight and ultraviolet light. • Do NOT refreeze the vaccine, once thawed. Refrigerator: +2 °C to +8 °C Up to 4.5 months (not exceeding expiry date) Opened vial (after first puncture of the vial) *: • During use,

sections.title: Thawing of frozen vaccine:

summary.text: Explains that frozen vials can be thawed in the refrigerator, taking about two hours for one vial and twelve for a carton, and must not be refrozen.

sections.extract: • Frozen vaccine vials may be thawed in the refrigerator (between +2 °C to +8 °C) This will take approximately 2 hours for a single vial and 12 hours for a carton of 10 vials.  NOTE: Do NOT refreeze thawed vaccine.

sections.title: Material needed for vaccination and supplies

summary.text: Lists supplies needed for vaccination, including suitable syringes and needles, antiseptic swabs, a sharps box, anaphylaxis kits, personal protective equipment and hand hygiene materials.

sections.extract: MATERIAL NEEDED FOR VACCINATION AND SUPPLIES • Syringe for vaccine administration (0.5 ml or 1 ml syringe with 0.1 ml graduations) with 23-gauge (or narrower) needle • Sterile single-use antiseptic swabs • Safety box for sharps disposal • Medical treatment kits to manage allergic reactions in the event of an acute anaphylactic reaction • Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for vaccinators and recipients (gown;

summary.text: A heading introducing the contraindications and precautions for the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine.

sections.title: Contraindications:

summary.text: States the single contraindication: a history of severe allergic reaction to any vaccine component.

sections.extract: • History of severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to any component of the vaccine.

sections.title: Precautions:

summary.text: Lists precautions for vaccination, namely acute febrile illness and bleeding risk in people on anticoagulants or with clotting disorders, and carries the job aid's page footer.

sections.extract: • Acute febrile illness • Individuals receiving anticoagulant therapy or those with thrombocytopenia or any coagulation disorder (such as haemophilia) because bleeding or bruising may occur following an intramuscular administration June 2021 Job aid for COVID-19 vaccine administration Janssen–Cilag International NV (Belgium) Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine June 2021 - Page 2 of 3

sections.title: Preparation and administration of vaccine

summary.text: Gives step-by-step instructions for preparing and giving the Janssen vaccine, from wearing protective equipment and screening the recipient (including a 14-day gap after other vaccines) to aseptic withdrawal of a 0.5 ml dose without dilution. It covers injecting into the deltoid, observing the person afterwards, recording the date, name and batch number, and reporting suspected adverse reactions.

sections.extract: PREPARATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF VACCINE  NOTE: The thawed vaccine is ready to use. Do NOT dilute the vaccine. Do NOT freeze the vaccine, once thawed. PREPARATION FOR VACCINE ADMINISTRATION ENVIRONMENT 1 • Be sure to wear correct personal protective equipment (PPE) before administering vaccines. sections.title: Management of anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions

summary.text: Advises that staff, equipment and medicines to manage anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions be on hand, with precautions against injury from fainting.

sections.extract: MANAGEMENT OF ANAPHYLAXIS AND ANXIETY-RELATED REACTIONS Events of anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions may occur. Make sure that a health-care worker competent in identifying and treating these reactions, and necessary equipment and medications, are available. Take precautions to avoid injury from fainting.

sections.title: Communication during vaccination visit

summary.text: Sets out suggested wording for the vaccination visit, covering vaccine benefits, screening questions, how the injection is given, the 15-minute observation period and common side effects. It also offers sample answers to typical concerns about side effects and conflicting information.

sections.title: Sources

summary.text: Advises telling vaccinated people to keep wearing masks, washing hands and keeping physical distance, and lists sources such as the EMA product information and WHO interim recommendations and background papers for the Janssen vaccine.

sections.extract: 6 Inform about the necessary follow-up Even after vaccination please continue to wear a face mask that covers your nose and mouth, wash your hands often and follow physical distancing advice. Together with vaccination, this gives you and others the best protection from catching the virus.” 8. SOURCES 1. COVID-19 COVID-19 vaccine Janssen. Amsterdam: European Medicines Agency; 2021
